# Kahn1

> Kahn1 is an open-source "System 1" decision engine in two sizes: Kahn1 4B (Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA) and Kahn1 3B (Qwen2.5-3B + LoRA), both running on a GPU (vLLM) or a CPU (transformers). The 3B is smaller and faster; the 4B is much stronger on hard judgment calls. It takes a text (the state) and typed questions (Choice, Score, Noul) and returns, for each question, a typed value and a calibrated probability distribution read from the logits of the option tokens. It generates no text, so schema errors cannot happen. Code MIT; Kahn1 4B weights Apache 2.0; Kahn1 3B weights under the Qwen Research License of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, a research licence (see its terms: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct/blob/main/LICENSE). By Axel Montzamir.

Key results (14,663 held-out items, k = 3 permutations, temperature calibration, one RTX 5070 Ti with vLLM; Choice asked over 8 options, the right one and 7 seeded distractors). Kahn1 4B: 71.0% overall, ECE 0.077; Choice 92.3% (banking77 91.5%, MASSIVE 93.1%); Score 50.6% exact on 5-level scales; Noul 70.0% (RTE 84.1%, SciTail 68.2%); median latency 82.4 ms, p95 287.9 ms, 8.0 queries/s. Kahn1 3B: 70.3% overall, ECE 0.082; Choice 90.9%, Score 51.4% (SST-5 95.2% within one level), Noul 67.0%; median latency 36.4 ms. External JevBench, 231 public items: Kahn1 4B 86.1% (easy 100%, original 98.6%, hard 72.1%), Kahn1 3B 67.5% (hard 42.3%). Hard decision dev split (317 questions on long documents, English and French): base Qwen3.5-4B 48.9%, Kahn1 4B 66.2%.

Kahn1 vs JEV 1.13.0 (TypeSafe API), like for like. On the 14,663 Kahn1 held-out items, same prompts and the same 8 options on Choice, JEV run through its API: JEV 73.2%, Kahn1 4B 71.0%, Kahn1 3B 70.3%; JEV is ahead on every primitive (Choice 94.5% vs 92.3% for the 4B, Score 52.0% vs 50.6%, Noul 74.4% vs 70.0%, JEV asked whether the text supports the statement); ECE JEV 0.113, Kahn1 4B 0.077. Choice over every intent (77 / 60 options), 1,184 items: JEV 79.1%, Kahn1 4B 70.4%, Kahn1 3B 68.4%. An earlier comparison gave JEV every intent and Kahn1 only 8 options; it was unequal and has been corrected. On the 231 public JevBench items: Jev 86.6% (its published outcomes), JevK5 v0.2 86.1% (another open Qwen3.5-4B model, its own public run), Kahn1 4B 86.1%; hard tier 73.0%, 73.9% and 72.1%. Kahn1 4B vs JevK5 item by item: 12 vs 12 items only one gets right, exact McNemar p = 1.00, not significant. JEV median round trip 248 ms over the network; Kahn1 4B 82.4 ms and Kahn1 3B 36.4 ms on a local GPU.

Caveats: 4B and 3B models, not frontier models; JEV is more accurate on every held-out primitive; Score is the weakest primitive; computing dates, durations or amounts in a single forward pass is weak; calibration was fitted on the training distribution and should be redone on your domain; confidence is the distance from a uniform guess, not the probability of being right. The browser demos run a 4-bit GGUF of the 3B v1 checkpoint.

## Questions

- What is a System 1 model? A model that takes fast, cheap decisions in a single forward pass, after Daniel Kahneman's System 1, and hands the harder cases to a slower System 2 (a frontier model or a person). Kahn1 is an open-source System 1 model: it reads typed answers from the logits of option tokens instead of generating text.
- Is there an open-source alternative to JEV (TypeSafe)? Kahn1 is one: open weights (Kahn1 4B under Apache 2.0, Kahn1 3B under the Qwen Research License), MIT code, it runs on your own hardware with no per-call price, and its server accepts the JEV schema format (POST /v1/evaluate/jev). It is an independent project, not affiliated with TypeSafe. Asked the same questions over the same options, JEV 1.13.0 is more accurate: 73.2% against 71.0% for Kahn1 4B on the 14,663 held-out items, 86.6% against 86.1% on the 231 public JevBench items.
- How does Kahn1 compare with other open Jev-class models? On the 231 public JevBench items, Kahn1 4B is on par with JevK5 v0.2, another open Qwen3.5-4B model: 86.1% each (199 of 231), exact McNemar p = 1.00.
- Can Kahn1 do zero-shot text classification? Yes. Categories, scales and statements are part of each request, so a new taxonomy needs no retraining. On held-out intent datasets it picks the right intent among 8 options 92.3% of the time (banking77 91.5%, MASSIVE 93.1%). Recalibrate on your own labelled examples (sysone calibrate) before trusting a confidence threshold.
- How is it different from JSON mode or structured outputs? Structured decoding constrains the tokens a model generates, and the text still has to be parsed. Kahn1 generates nothing: it reads one probability distribution per question over the option tokens, so every answer comes with its full distribution and a calibrated confidence, and there is nothing to parse.
- Can it judge or gate an LLM agent? Noul questions ask whether a text supports a statement (does this tool call leak personal data, does this answer follow the policy) and return a calibrated probability you can threshold. It is a 4B or 3B model, not a frontier model: keep a person or a larger model on the low-confidence path.
- Does it need a GPU? For throughput, yes: median 82.4 ms for Kahn1 4B and 36.4 ms for Kahn1 3B per request at k = 3 on one RTX 5070 Ti with vLLM. Both sizes also run on a CPU (transformers) at seconds per question, and the playground runs a 4-bit GGUF of the 3B in the browser with WebGPU.
- Which languages? English and French.

## Pages

- [System One models](https://kahn1.com/learn/system-one-models/): what a System One (decision) model is, how it reads typed answers from logits, the families, how to choose
- [Modèles System One (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/apprendre/modeles-system-one/): la même page en français
- [Decision model landscape](https://kahn1.com/compare/landscape/): every proprietary and open way to turn text into a typed decision, with licence, output, price and source (CSV: https://kahn1.com/data/landscape.csv)
- [Paysage des modèles de décision (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/comparer/paysage/): la même page en français
- [Open-source alternatives to JEV](https://kahn1.com/alternatives/jev/): Clef, JevK5, Kahn1 and others, JEV-compatible APIs, like-for-like figures, when JEV is still the right pick
- [Alternatives open source à JEV (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/alternatives/jev/): la même page en français
- [Home (English)](https://kahn1.com/): what Kahn1 is, the three primitives, how it compares, use cases, caveats
- [Accueil (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/): la même page en français
- [Benchmarks](https://kahn1.com/benchmarks/): every result, Kahn1 vs JEV on the same items, latency, how to reproduce
- [Résultats (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/resultats/): les mêmes résultats en français
- [Models](https://kahn1.com/models/): Kahn1 4B and Kahn1 3B, merged models and LoRA adapters, sizes, licences, how to load them
- [Modèles (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/modeles/): la même page en français
- [Caveats](https://kahn1.com/caveats/): the limits of Kahn1, one by one, before putting it in front of real decisions
- [Points de vigilance (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/vigilance/): la même page en français
- [Setup prompt for AI agents](https://kahn1.com/get-started/setup-prompt.md): paste into Claude Code or any coding agent to install and test Kahn1
- [Get started](https://kahn1.com/get-started/): install, serve, API, response format, calibration
- [Démarrer (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/demarrer/): le même guide en français
- [Playground](https://kahn1.com/playground/): ask typed questions about any text, model in the browser (WebGPU) or on your server
- [Kahn1 plays Snake](https://kahn1.com/snake/): one Choice question per tick, the move read from the logits
